title: Kc calculations and Q; Oxidation states and half-equations
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AQA A-level Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: RX01#t1 term and clue written for the game; RX01#t4 term and clue written for the game; RX01#t3 term and clue written for the game; EQ03#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: EQ03#N.6a, RX01#N.6a, EQ03#N.8, RX01#N.11a, EQ03#N.14a, RX01#N.14.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Redox
items.clue: A reaction in which loss and gain of electrons happen together.

items.label: Reduction
items.clue: Gain of electrons, as when each O atom goes from 0 to −2 during rusting.

items.label: Reducing agent
items.clue: The reactant that gives electrons away, like Zn in Zn + Cu²⁺ → Zn²⁺ + Cu.

items.label: Reaction quotient Q
items.clue: Compared with K to predict direction: if it is smaller, there is a net forward change.

questions.stem: N₂O₄(g) ⇌ 2NO₂(g). N₂O₄ is placed in a sealed vessel at an initial concentration of 0.200 mol dm⁻³ and the mixture is allowed to reach equilibrium at constant temperature. At equilibrium, [NO₂] = 0.080 mol dm⁻³. What is the value of Kc at this temperature?
questions.explanation: 0.080 of NO₂ uses 0.040 of N₂O₄, so [N₂O₄] = 0.160 mol dm⁻³. Kc = 0.080² ÷ 0.160 = 0.040 mol dm⁻³.

questions.stem: Chlorine reacts with aqueous iron(II) ions: 2Fe²⁺(aq) + Cl₂(aq) → 2Fe³⁺(aq) + 2Cl⁻(aq). Which species is the oxidising agent in this reaction?

options.text: Fe²⁺, since it loses electrons and so is itself oxidised
Cl₂, since it gains electrons and so is itself reduced
Cl⁻, since it is the species holding the gained electrons
None, since no species here gains or loses any oxygen atoms

questions.explanation: Chlorine's oxidation number falls from 0 to −1: each Cl₂ gains two electrons from Fe²⁺. The species that accepts electrons is the oxidising agent.

questions.stem: 0.400 mol SO₂ and 0.200 mol O₂ are sealed in a 2.00 dm³ vessel. At equilibrium the vessel contains 0.300 mol SO₃. What is Kc for 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2SO₃(g)?
In acidic solution, MnO₄⁻(aq) is reduced to Mn²⁺(aq) and Fe²⁺(aq) is oxidised to Fe³⁺(aq). In the balanced overall redox equation, what amount of Fe²⁺ reacts with 1 mol of MnO₄⁻?
questions.explanation: Mn goes from +7 to +2, so each MnO₄⁻ gains 5 electrons; each Fe²⁺ loses 1. The iron half-equation is multiplied by 5.

questions.stem: Back to the sealed flask: H₂(g) + I₂(g) ⇌ 2HI(g). It was filled with 0.500 mol H₂ and 0.500 mol I₂ and no HI, in a 2.00 dm³ flask. It has now reached equilibrium and holds 0.800 mol HI. What is Kc at this temperature?
questions.explanation: 0.800 mol HI uses 0.400 mol each of H₂ and I₂, leaving 0.100 mol each. Kc = 0.800² ÷ (0.100 × 0.100) = 64. Two terms on top, two below: the volume and the units cancel.

questions.stem: In the thermite reaction, aluminium reacts with iron(III) oxide: Fe₂O₃(s) + 2Al(s) → Al₂O₃(s) + 2Fe(l). What happens to the iron?

options.text: It loses electrons: iron is always oxidised when it reacts, as it does in rusting.
It gains electrons: its oxidation number falls from +3 to 0, and aluminium supplies them.
It loses electrons to aluminium, since aluminium gains the oxygen during the reaction.
It gains electrons: its oxidation number falls from +6 to 0, as Fe₂O₃ has two Fe atoms.
